source_edition: Final journal edition, 2021, pages 491-499; one archive cover.

claims.label: Theorem 1.1
claims.qualification: Full typed automorphism group, not the specified marked group; accepted rank-four thin geometry.
claims.attribution: Existing reviewed project counterexample; source theorem belongs to Leemans and Tranchida.

claims.label: Proposition 2.1
claims.qualification: The general group action need not be faithful; object and incident-pair transitivity are proved.
claims.attribution: Source attributes the construction to Tits (1956), reference [9].

claims.label: Theorem 2.2
claims.qualification: The sufficient part needed here is proved directly; no acquisition of the entire cited monograph.
claims.attribution: Source [1], Buekenhout and Cohen, Diagram geometry, Corollary 1.8.13.

claims.label: Theorem 3.1
claims.qualification: Expressly quoted earlier theorem, not a new result of L029; neither used to certify nor refuted by our counterexamples.
claims.attribution: Source [6], Fernandes, Leemans and Weiss, Highly symmetric hypertopes, Theorem 4.6.

claims.label: Theorem 3.3
claims.qualification: Expressly quoted earlier theorem, not a new result of L029; neither used to certify nor refuted by our counterexamples.
claims.attribution: Source [6], Fernandes, Leemans and Weiss, Highly symmetric hypertopes, Theorem 7.1.

claims.label: Corollary 3.4
claims.qualification: Expressly quoted earlier theorem, not a new result of L029; neither used to certify nor refuted by our counterexamples.
claims.attribution: Source [6], Fernandes, Leemans and Weiss, Highly symmetric hypertopes, Corollary 7.2.

claims.label: Construction 3.2
claims.qualification: Nondegenerate independent marking; inversion relates source right cosets to left cosets.
claims.attribution: Original construction and C+ framework are retained from the source and its predecessors.

claims.label: Chirality implies thinness
claims.qualification: Literal geometry definition does not include firmness; corrected firm version holds.
claims.attribution: Seven-object example supplied by the project, without a priority claim.

claims.label: Theorem 4.1
claims.qualification: Seven-object example refutes the literal unrestricted assertion. Firm version is proved by normalization.
claims.attribution: Source normalization idea retained with explicit hypotheses; new project example is separate from the principal refutation.

claims.label: Proposition 4.2
claims.qualification: Seven-object example refutes the literal unrestricted assertion. Firm version is proved by normalization.
claims.attribution: Source normalization idea retained with explicit hypotheses; new project example is separate from the principal refutation.

claims.label: Lemma 4.3
claims.qualification: Injective incidence homomorphism, object-surjectivity criterion; all-surjectivity implication shown for the geometry interface used here.
claims.attribution: Source [1], Lemma 1.8.9 (iii-v); direct proof supplied for required interfaces.

claims.label: Remark 4.4
claims.qualification: Bijective incidence homomorphism need not have an incidence-preserving inverse.

claims.label: Lemma 4.5
claims.qualification: Coset geometry and transitivity on the smaller flag type are explicit.
claims.attribution: Source normalization proof reworked using retained project proof bank.

claims.label: Proposition 4.6
claims.qualification: C2^2 cone, seven objects, eight J-flags, orbit size four, singleton internal residue. Smaller-type transitivity repairs condition (2).
claims.attribution: Previously retained project counterexample, not the new seven-object chirality example.

claims.label: Proposition 4.7
claims.qualification: Displayed bound allows rank one, where the accepted thin example refutes it. The preceding paragraph excludes rank one. No unrestricted higher-rank repair claimed.
claims.attribution: Source generation idea retained with specified proper-flag transitivity and residue rank at least two.

claims.label: Lemma 4.8
claims.qualification: Nontrivial cyclic rank-two C+ marking. Rank-at-least-three canonical neighbours are proved; general rank-at-least-four firmness remains unproved.
claims.attribution: Source canonical-neighbour construction retained; rank-two correction supplied by the project.

claims.label: Corollary 4.9
claims.qualification: Nontrivial cyclic rank-two C+ marking. Rank-at-least-three canonical neighbours are proved; general rank-at-least-four firmness remains unproved.
claims.attribution: Source canonical-neighbour construction retained; rank-two correction supplied by the project.

claims.label: Example 4.10 and Figure 1
claims.qualification: Two matchings for arbitrary nontrivial cyclic order. Applies to normalized residues under the explicit action hypothesis. Source example continues on page 498.
claims.attribution: Source cyclic illustration retained and explained in the prior project proof bank.

claims.label: Proposition 4.11
claims.qualification: Every nondegenerate rank-three marking gives a firm residually connected geometry; no full group computation required.
claims.attribution: Original result recovered using the retained normalization argument.

unproved_corrected_variants: General firmness for C+ coset geometries in rank at least four without additional action hypotheses.
